[ce] Levenberg Marquardt.vi

Owning Palette: Curve Fitting

This VI uses the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm to determine the least squares set of coefficients that best fit the set of input data points (X, Y) as expressed by a nonlinear function y = f(x, a) where a is the set of coefficients.

Click the parameters for more information

 

VC Handle. If a model contains independent variable(s) to be evaluated in the formula, pass a handle of the variable context that contains desired variables to this control. Otherwise, keep it unwired.
Standard Deviation. Standard Deviation is the array of standard deviations, sigma[i], for data point (x[i],y[i]).  

If the standard deviations are all equal or if they are unknown, leave this control unwired and the standard deviations will be set to 1.0.
X specifies the array of independent values.
Y specifies the array of dependent values, or the observations.
Initial Guess Coefficients. Initial Guess Coefficients is your initial guess of the solution coefficients.
max iteration max iteration is the maximum executing iterations used in the nonlinear fit algorithm.

If max iterations is exceeded and a solution is not found, this VI will return an error.  At that point, you must increase max iterations, adjust the Initial Guess Coefficients, or change the target function.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
model description.
model. A string describing the model equation.
Parameters. An array of strings representing the unknown parameters.
x. A string describing the independent variable.
Covariance. Covariance is the matrix of covariances C.

c[j,k] is the covariance between a[j] and a[k], and c[]j,j] is the variance of a[j].
Best Fit Coefficients. Best Fit Coefficients is the array of coefficients that minimize the chi-square error between the solution vector and the observed Y values.
Best Fit. Best Fit is the fitted data z[i] = f(x[i],A), where A is the set of Best Fit Coefficients.
mse mse is the chi-squared error between the Best Fit and the observed Y values.
ticks.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
iterations.
